flow.costPlain: What each payment costs PayPal to run: $4,252M of transaction expense (card-network and processing fees) plus $390M of transaction and credit losses on its loans.

opex.note: Support staff and the cost of running payment operations.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Marketing, and winning merchants and users.

opex.name: Technology and development
opex.note: Building and running the PayPal and Venmo platforms.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company: finance, legal, risk and offices.

opex.name: Restructuring and other
opex.note: Severance and reshaping costs as PayPal works through its transformation plan.

oneTimers: GAAP results include gains on PayPal's strategic investment portfolio and crypto assets worth about $0.10 of EPS in the quarter, versus a roughly $0.04 drag in Q4 2024 — a swing that explains much of the GAAP profit jump.
Restructuring and other charges were $80M in the quarter as PayPal reshapes the organization; the board also announced Enrique Lores as the next President and CEO alongside these results.
otherDetail: Other income (expense), net was +$116M, including gains on PayPal's strategic investment portfolio.

segments.name: Transaction revenues
segments.note: The cut PayPal takes on every payment it processes — $475B of payment volume flowed through in the quarter, up 9%, across 6.8 billion transactions.

segments.name: Revenues from other value added services
segments.note: Interest on customer balances, partner fees and other services around the core payment.

takeaways.text: Total payment volume rose 9% to $475.1B and transactions rose 2% to 6.8 billion, with 439 million active accounts.
takeaways.title: The payment pipes keep growing

takeaways.text: Revenue grew 4%: transaction revenues +3% and value-added services +10%. Transaction margin dollars rose 3% to $4.0B — the core business grew, just slowly.
takeaways.title: Steady, slower growth

takeaways.text: GAAP EPS rose 38% to $1.53, including a roughly $0.10 boost from PayPal's strategic investment portfolio and crypto assets, versus a $0.04 drag a year ago. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.23.
takeaways.title: Investment gains flattered EPS

verdict: PayPal moved $475B of payments (+9%) and grew revenue 4% to $8.7B, while GAAP net income rose 28% to $1.4B — helped by gains in its investment portfolio — as the board named a new CEO to fix branded checkout execution.
